misconception_pool.misconception: Masking tape or transparent office tape holds drawing paper to a drafting board just as cleanly as drafting tape.
misconception_pool.fact: Standard office and masking tapes have aggressive adhesives that tear paper fibers upon removal, unlike low-tack drafting tape.

misconception_pool.misconception: Title block guidelines should be erased after completing single-stroke Gothic lettering so the block looks clean.
misconception_pool.fact: Light construction guidelines drawn with a hard 4H or 6H lead remain barely visible on the sheet and should never be erased.

misconception_pool.misconception: Border lines and construction guidelines use the same pencil lead hardness and line weight across a drawing sheet.
misconception_pool.fact: Borders require a thick, dark line drawn with a softer F or HB lead, whereas guidelines need an ultra-light 4H or 6H pencil.

misconception_pool.misconception: Standard ANSI B-size architectural and engineering sheets measure exactly twice the width and length of an A-size sheet.
misconception_pool.fact: An ANSI B-size sheet measures 11 by 17 inches, which doubles only the short 8.5-inch side of an 8.5 by 11-inch A-size sheet.

requirements.req_text: Using the formatted sheet of paper you prepared for your manual project, produce a pencil drawing as it would be used for manufacturing. Fill in all title block information. The manual drawing may be any one of the following drawing types: (a) Architectural: Make a scale drawing of an architectural project. The architectural drawing may be a floor plan; electrical, plumbing, or mechanical service plan; elevation plan; or landscaping plan. Use an architect's scale and show dimensions to communicate the actual size of features. Include any important sectional drawings, notes, and considerations necessary for construction. Properly print a bill of materials for at least three of the raw materials or components in the project. (b) Mechanical: Make a scale drawing of some mechanical device or interesting object. The mechanical drawing may be of the orthographic (third-angle) or isometric style. Use an engineer's scale and show dimensions to communicate the actual size of features. Include any important sectional drawings, notes, and manufacturing considerations. Properly print a bill of materials for at least three of the raw materials or components in the assembly. (c) Electrical: Draw a simple schematic of a radio or electronic circuit. Properly print a bill of materials including all of the major electrical components used in the circuit. Use standard drawing symbols to represent the electronic components.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Visit a facility or industry workplace where drafting is part of the business. If CAD is used, find out what software is used and how and why it was chosen. (2) Ask about the drafting services provided. Ask who uses the designs produced in the drafting area and how those designs are used. Discuss how the professionals who perform drafting cooperate with other individuals in the drafting area and other areas of the business. (3) Ask how important the role of drafting is to producing the end product or service that this business supplies. Find out how drafting contributes to the company's end product or service. (b) Using resources you find on your own such as at the library and on the internet (with your parent or guardian's permission), learn more about the drafting trade and discuss the following with your counselor. Tell how the advent of CAD has changed the media used, and discuss how these changes affect the storage or reproduction of drawings. (3) Discuss whether the types of media have changed such that there are new uses the drawings, or other outputs, produced by designers. patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Drafting Requirement 1, how does third-angle orthographic projection represent a three-dimensional object on a flat drawing sheet, and how are object lines distinguished from hidden lines?
options: A. It shows only a single artistic watercolor painting of the building with no measurements, using dotted lines for all outer walls.
B. It places the right-side view above the top view and uses thick wavy freehand lines for invisible interior cavities.
C. It stretches all vertical edges at a forty-five degree angle without a scale ratio and draws centerlines with solid heavy ink.
D. It aligns the front, top, and right-side views at 90-degree projection angles to show exact scaled dimensions.
choices: A. It shows only a single artistic watercolor painting of the building with no measurements, using dotted lines for all outer walls.
B. It places the right-side view above the top view and uses thick wavy freehand lines for invisible interior cavities.
C. It stretches all vertical edges at a forty-five degree angle without a scale ratio and draws centerlines with solid heavy ink.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. It aligns the front, top, and right-side views at 90-degree projection angles to show exact scaled dimensions, using thick solid lines for visible edges and medium dashed lines for hidden internal features.
